statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14669 (PostgreSQL to_char heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code): a long POSIX time zone abbreviation overflows the output buffer of to_char(timestamptz). PostgreSQL fixed it in 16.15 for major version 16: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14669/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release, and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, list this CVE. The fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/3d724bf4fde67a2931733a5143b7d6c12b23990c on master (Security: CVE-2026-14669, back-patched through 14), adds a length check with the error "time zone format value too long" to DCH_to_char in src/backend/utils/adt/formatting.c. On the REL_16_STABLE branch the same formatting.c change arrived in https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/5dbeb69bcb0313f20731f43b682e04a663f39d27, whose commit message describes an unrelated walreceiver fix and does not name this CVE; the check is absent from formatting.c at tag REL_16_14 and present at REL_16_15. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-14669 under 16.15-r0 in its secfixes. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch and the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball, and none of the patches in the APKBUILD at that commit touches formatting.c. We read /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres in every published postgresql16 package for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0) on x86_64 and aarch64: 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.13 and 16.14 and lack the "time zone format value too long" message, while 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report 16.15 and 16.16 and contain it. 16.15-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14669, a heap buffer overflow in to_char(timestamptz) through a long POSIX time zone abbreviation, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14669/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14669. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
